label: archaeal cannula
definition: An extracellular hollow tubular archaeal cell projection, characterized in Pyrodictium species, that extends from the cell envelope as a proteinaceous filament and forms networks between cells.

label: archaeal-type flagellum
definition: A non-membrane-bounded archaeal motility organelle, also called the archaellum, whose ATP-powered membrane motor rotates one or more glycosylated type-IV-pilin-like archaellin filaments outside the cell to drive swimming.

label: attachment organelle
definition: A membrane-bounded polar cell extension in Mycoplasma species that concentrates cytadherence and cytoskeletal proteins for host-cell attachment, gliding motility, and organelle-linked cell division.

label: attachment organelle membrane
definition: The membrane surrounding the attachment organelle.

label: bacterial-type flagellum
definition: The rotary motility organelle of bacteria: a long helical filament of flagellin joined by a flexible hook to a basal body that spans the cell envelope. The basal body houses a rotor (MS and C rings) driven by membrane-embedded stator units that convert ion flow (H+ or Na+) into torque; the flagellar type III export apparatus at its base secretes the axial subunits. Not homologous to the archaeal archaellum or the eukaryotic cilium.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body
definition: The basal cell-envelope substructure of a bacterial flagellum, consisting of a rod, a series of rings, Mot stator proteins, the switch complex, and the proximal flagellum-specific type III export apparatus.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, C ring
definition: The cytoplasmic FliG/FliM/FliN switch ring of the bacterial flagellar basal body, assembled on the MS ring to form the rotor face that receives torque from Mot/Pom stator units and changes rotational bias in response to phosphorylated CheY.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, distal rod
definition: The portion of the central rod of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body that is distal to the cell membrane; spans most of the distance between the inner and outer membranes.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, distal rod, L ring
definition: One of the rings of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body; anchors the basal body to the outer membrane.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, distal rod, P ring
definition: One of the rings of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body; anchors the basal body to the peptidoglycan layer.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, MS ring
definition: One of the rings of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body; a double-flanged ring that anchors the basal body to the cytoplasmic membrane.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, proximal rod
definition: The portion of the central rod of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body that is proximal to the cell membrane; the proximal rod connects the distal rod to the flagellar motor.

label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, rod
definition: The central portion of the bacterial-type flagellar basal body, which spans the periplasm and threads through the rings.

label: bacterial-type flagellum filament
definition: The long (approximately 20 nm), thin external structure of the bacterial-type flagellum, which acts as a propeller.

label: bacterial-type flagellum filament cap
definition: The proteinaceous structure at the distal tip of the bacterial-type flagellar filament.

label: bacterial-type flagellum hook
definition: The portion of the bacterial-type flagellum that connects the filament to the basal body.

label: bacterial-type flagellum hook-filament junction
definition: The FlgK/FlgL hook-associated protein junction at the distal end of the bacterial-type flagellar hook that couples the flexible hook to the flagellin filament and buffers mechanical stress while initiating filament assembly.

label: bacterial-type flagellum motor
definition: A bacterial flagellar basal-body motor composed of an MS-ring/C-ring rotor complex and one or more Mot/Pom-family stator complexes in the cytoplasmic membrane that convert ion flow into rotary torque and bias clockwise or counterclockwise output.

label: bacterial-type flagellum rotor complex
definition: The bacterial flagellar basal-body rotor built from the membrane-anchored FliF MS ring and the cytoplasmic FliG/FliM/FliN C ring, which together receive torque from stator units, rotate the axial rod, and bias clockwise or counterclockwise motor output.

label: bacterial-type flagellum secretion apparatus
definition: A flagellum-specific type III export apparatus at the cytoplasmic side of the bacterial MS ring that uses a FlhA/FlhB/FliP/FliQ/FliR membrane export gate and a FliH/FliI/FliJ cytoplasmic ATPase complex to export rod, hook, and filament subunits through the growing flagellum.

label: bacterial-type flagellum stator complex
definition: An ion-driven membrane complex in the bacterial flagellar motor, typically with five A subunits surrounding two B subunits, that transduces proton or sodium flow into torque on the flagellar rotor and anchors to the cell wall through the B subunits.

label: ciliary membrane
definition: The portion of the plasma membrane surrounding a cilium.

label: ciliary transition zone
definition: A region of the cilium between the basal body and proximal segment that is characterized by Y-shaped assemblages that connect axonemal microtubules to the ciliary membrane. The ciliary transition zone appears to function as a gate that controls ciliary membrane composition and separates the cytosol from the ciliary plasm.

label: cilium
definition: A specialized eukaryotic organelle that consists of a filiform extrusion of the cell surface and of some cytoplasmic parts; it is largely bounded by an extrusion of the plasma membrane, contains a longitudinal microtubule array, and is anchored to a basal body.

label: curli
definition: Extracellular amyloid fibers assembled from CsgA by the Csg secretion and nucleation machinery that form a pilus subtype in enteric biofilm matrices.

label: hamus
definition: An archaeal cell-surface appendage composed of proteinaceous helical filaments with periodic prickles and a terminal grappling hook, used by Candidatus Altarchaeum hamiconexum cells to attach to biotic and abiotic surfaces.

label: haptonema
definition: An elongated, plasma-membrane-bounded, microtubule-supported appendage of haptophyte algae that emerges from the flagellar pole and can coil rapidly during haptonemal motility or participate in particle capture.

label: mastigoneme
definition: A hair-like structure covering the flagella found in some algae (heterokonts and cryptophytes). It is approximately 15 nm in diameter, and usually consist of a tubular shaft that itself terminates in smaller hairs. It is composed of glycoproteins and, likely, carbohydrates. Mastigonemes may assist in locomotion by increasing the surface area of a flagellum.

label: OmcE cytochrome nanowire
definition: An extracellular Geobacter sulfurreducens cytochrome nanowire assembled from OmcE tetraheme c-type cytochrome subunits and resolved by cryo-EM as a helical filament whose hemes pack within the filament core.

label: OmcS cytochrome nanowire
definition: An extracellular electrically conductive Geobacter sulfurreducens PCA filament assembled as a helical array of OmcS six-heme c-type cytochrome monomers whose stacked hemes provide a path for long-range electron transport.

label: OmcZ cytochrome nanowire
definition: An extracellular electrically conductive Geobacter sulfurreducens filament assembled from the octaheme c-type cytochrome OmcZ; each subunit contributes a branched heme arrangement with a surface-exposed heme site to the cytochrome polymer.

label: P pilus
definition: A chaperone-usher adhesive pilus of uropathogenic Escherichia coli built from a PapA helical rod, a PapG-PapF-PapE tip fibrillum, a PapK adaptor that bridges the fibrillum to the rod, and a basal PapH terminator. The PapD chaperone delivers subunits to the PapC usher, which assembles the pilus, and the distal PapG adhesin binds host glycolipid receptors.

label: paraflagellar rod
definition: A large lattice-like axial structure found in some flagellated protists which extends alongside the axoneme. Protein components of the paraflagellar rod are likely implicated, among other, in adenine nucleotide signaling and metabolism, and in calcium signaling.

label: periplasmic flagellum
definition: A bacterial-type flagellar appendage of spirochetes whose filaments reside in the periplasmic space between the cytoplasmic and outer membranes, attach near the cell poles, and rotate to deform the cell cylinder for motility.

label: pilus
definition: A proteinaceous hair-like appendage on the surface of bacteria ranging from 2-8 nm in diameter.

label: prostheca
definition: A tubular projection of the bacterial cell envelope and cytoplasm that extends away from the main cell body in prosthecate bacteria. In stalked Caulobacter cells, the prostheca contains the inner membrane, peptidoglycan and outer membrane layers of the Gram-negative envelope and supports stalk-specific compartmentalization and nutrient uptake.

label: stalk crossband
definition: A disk-like multiprotein diffusion barrier that spans the Caulobacter stalk cross-section. StpABCD-containing stalk crossbands partition the prostheca into compartments by limiting exchange of soluble and membrane proteins between the cell body and stalk segments.

label: Tad pilus
definition: A tight-adherence subtype of type IV pilus that extends and retracts from a bacterial cell pole. In Caulobacter vibrioides, Tad pili are polar PilA filaments whose dynamic activity promotes surface sensing, surface colonization and holdfast-dependent permanent attachment.

label: type I pilus
definition: A chaperone-usher bacterial pilus assembled from a helical FimA rod tipped by the adaptor subunits FimG and FimF and the mannose-binding FimH adhesin. In Escherichia coli, the type I pilus is polymerized through the outer-membrane FimD usher and terminated by a basal FimI subunit that anchors the completed rod to the assembly platform.

label: type IV pilus
definition: A dynamic bacterial surface filament assembled from type IV pilins by an inner-membrane ATPase machinery. Reversible extension and retraction can generate force for twitching motility, adhesion, surface sensing, and DNA uptake.

label: actin cortical patch
definition: An endocytic patch formed from branched actin filaments just beneath the plasma membrane that assembles, moves, and disassembles rapidly.

label: actomyosin contractile ring
definition: A cytokinetic cytoskeletal ring composed of actin filaments, myosin, and accessory proteins that assembles beneath the plasma membrane and constricts during cell division.

label: AlfA filament
definition: A plasmid-encoded bacterial actin-like cytoskeletal filament assembled from AlfA ATPases that supports segregation of pLS32-family plasmids in Bacillus subtilis.

label: axoneme
definition: A microtubule-based bundle with associated proteins that forms the core of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum.

label: bactofilin filament
definition: A bacterial cytoskeletal filament assembled from bactofilin proteins that forms beta-helical scaffolds for species-specific cellular organization processes, including polar stalk biogenesis in Caulobacter vibrioides.

label: bilobe structure
definition: A cytoskeletal structure in some kinetoplastid species linking the structures of the ciliary pocket collar and the flagellum attachment zone.

label: BtubAB bacterial microtubule
definition: A bacterial cytoskeletal microtubule assembled from BtubA and BtubB tubulin homologs that form tube-like filaments in Prosthecobacter cells and in purified BtubA/B reactions.

label: CetZ filament
definition: An archaeal tubulin-like cytoskeletal filament assembled from CetZ proteins that forms dynamic envelope-associated structures and supports cell-shape remodeling such as rod development in Haloferax volcanii.

label: ciliary basal body
definition: A membrane-tethered, short cylindrical array of microtubules and associated proteins found at the base of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum that derives from a centriole, anchors the cilium and nucleates axonemal microtubule growth.

label: ciliary pocket collar
definition: A constriction site at the junction of the plasma, flagellar and flagellar pocket membranes where the flagellum emerges from the cell body. Observed in some unicellular eukaryotic species such as Chlamydomonas, Giardia and Trypanosoma.

label: conoid
definition: A spiral cytoskeletal structure located at the apical end of the apical complex in some apicomplexan parasites. Fibers form a left-handed spiral, and are comprised of tubulin protofilaments organized in a ribbon-like structure that differs from the conventional tubular structure characteristic of microtubules.

label: crescentin filament
definition: A bacterial intermediate filament-like cytoskeletal filament assembled from crescentin that localizes along the inner curvature of Caulobacter vibrioides cells and helps maintain their curved cell shape.

label: cytoophidium
definition: A filamentous, membrane-less subcellular structure composed primarily of polymerized metabolic enzymes, most notably cytidine triphosphate synthase (CTPS). Cytoophidia are evolutionarily conserved structures found across archaea, bacteria, and eukaryotes.

label: eisosome filament
definition: A filamentous cortical structure formed, in S. pombe, by the eisosome component Pil1.

label: flagellum attachment zone
definition: A network of cytoskeletal and membranous connections responsible for the lateral attachment of the cilium to the cell body in some trypanosomatid species.

label: MamK filament
definition: An actin-like bacterial cytoskeletal filament assembled from MamK proteins that runs alongside magnetosomes in magnetotactic bacteria and helps organize the organelles into chains.

label: microtubule
definition: Any of the long, generally straight, hollow tubes of internal diameter 12-15 nm and external diameter 24 nm found in a wide variety of eukaryotic cells; each consists (usually) of 13 protofilaments of polymeric tubulin, staggered in such a manner that the tubulin monomers are arranged in a helical pattern on the microtubular surface, and with the alpha/beta axes of the tubulin subunits parallel to the long axis of the tubule; exist in equilibrium with pool of tubulin monomers and can be rapidly assembled or disassembled in response to physiological stimuli; concerned with force generation, e.g. in the spindle.

label: mitotic spindle
definition: A spindle that forms as part of mitosis. Mitotic and meiotic spindles contain distinctive complements of proteins associated with microtubules.

label: MreB filament
definition: The actin-like cytoskeletal filament of rod-shaped bacteria. MreB polymerises into short membrane-associated filaments that circle the cell at an angle to its long axis and move processively around it, carrying the elongasome — the peptidoglycan synthases that widen the sidewall — so that new wall material is inserted where the filaments travel. It is a homologue of eukaryotic actin by fold, not by sequence identity.

label: ParM filament
definition: A plasmid-encoded bacterial actin-like cytoskeletal filament assembled from ParM that is captured and stabilized by ParR-parC plasmid-centromere complexes to support active segregation of low-copy-number plasmids such as Escherichia coli R1.

label: PhuZ spindle
definition: A phage-encoded tubulin-like cytoskeletal spindle assembled from PhuZ polymers that positions the jumbo-phage nucleus in infected bacterial cells.

label: polar ring of apical complex
definition: An electron dense ring at the most anterior position of the apical complex, from which the conoid fibers originate; formed during an invasive life cycle stage of an apicomplexan parasite.

label: septin ring
definition: A tight ring-shaped septin-based cytoskeletal structure that forms at the cell cortex in the division plane, including the bud-neck septin ring of budding yeast and related fungal septin rings at septation sites.

label: spindle pole body
definition: The microtubule-organizing center in fungi, functionally homologous to the animal centrosome.

label: tripartite attachment complex
definition: A three-part cytoskeletal structure in kinetoplastid species linking mitochondrial DNA organised in a kinetoplast through the mitochondrial membranes to the basal body.

label: TubZ filament
definition: A plasmid-encoded bacterial tubulin-like cytoskeletal filament assembled from TubZ GTPase subunits that supports pBtoxis plasmid partitioning in Bacillus thuringiensis.

label: ventral disc
definition: Specialized organelle found in Giardia species (trophozoite stage) and characterized by a spiral array of microtubules and microtubule-associated structures including dorsal microribbons and crossbridges. The edge of the ventral disc narrows into a lateral crest. The ventral disk mediates mechanical attachment of the trophozoite to the host's intestinal wall, and contains the contractile proteins actinin, alpha-actinin, myosin, and tropomyosin working towards contraction of the disk involved in adherence.

label: ventral disc crossbridge
definition: A fibrous structure that horizontally links adjacent dorsal microribbons in the ventral disc of Giardia species trophozoites.

label: ventral disc dorsal microribbon
definition: Trilaminar structure extending perpendicularly into the cytoplasm along the length of ventral disc microtubules in Giardia species (trophozoite stage). Constituents of dorsal microribbons (also called dorsal ribbons or microribbons) include alpha-coiled-helix proteins approximately 29 to 38 kDa in size. These proteins line the edges of the microribbons but are not found in microtubules. Tubulins are not found in microribbons.

label: ventral disc lateral crest
definition: A fibrillar repetitive structure that surrounds the edge of the ventral disc in Giardia species trophozoites.

label: ventral disc microtubule array
definition: A part of the ventral disc of Giardia species (trophozoite stage) consisting of a spiral array of microtubules linked to the ventral membrane. These microtubules form the base of the ventral disc dorsal microribbons that extend nearly perpendicular from the membrane.

label: ventral disc overlap zone
definition: A region of the ventral disc of Giardia species (trophozoite stage) where two portions of the same array of microtubules overlap (the microtubule array makes a complete circle and overlaps on itself).

label: ventral disc supernumerary microtubule array
definition: A partial left-handed spiral array of microtubules that lies generally dorsal to the main ventral disc microtubule array in Giardia species trophozoites.

label: divisome complex
definition: The membrane-associated protein machine that constricts a dividing bacterial cell. It is organised by the FtsZ ring — treadmilling filaments of the tubulin homologue FtsZ tethered to the inner membrane — which positions and moves the septal peptidoglycan synthases that build the division septum.

label: elongasome
definition: The sidewall peptidoglycan-synthesis machine of rod-shaped bacteria, also called the Rod complex. A SEDS-family glycosyltransferase (RodA) works with a class B penicillin-binding protein (PBP2) to polymerise and crosslink new wall material into the cylinder, while MreC, MreD and RodZ couple the complex to MreB filaments, which distribute it around the circumference. It is the elongation counterpart of the divisome.

label: chlorosome baseplate antenna complex
definition: A bacteriochlorophyll a-CsmA light-harvesting protein-pigment array on one face of green bacterial chlorosomes that accepts excitation energy from chlorosome bacteriochlorophyll aggregates and couples it toward membrane reaction-center complexes.

label: chromatophore cytochrome bc1 complex
definition: A purple-bacterial chromatophore membrane cytochrome bc1 protein complex that oxidizes quinol from the chromatophore quinone pool and returns electrons toward reaction-center antenna cores through soluble cytochrome c2 during cyclic photosynthetic electron transport.

label: cytochrome b6f complex
definition: A thylakoid membrane protein complex that oxidizes plastoquinol, reduces a downstream soluble electron carrier for photosystem I, and contributes to proton translocation during oxygenic photosynthetic electron transport.

label: LH2 peripheral light-harvesting antenna complex
definition: A peripheral bacteriochlorophyll-containing light-harvesting antenna protein complex of purple bacterial chromatophore membranes that broadens the photosynthetic absorption cross-section and transfers excitation energy toward RC-LH1 reaction-center core complexes.

label: light-harvesting complex
definition: A protein-pigment complex that may be closely or peripherally associated to photosynthetic reaction centers that participate in harvesting and transferring radiant energy to the reaction center.

label: phycobilisome
definition: A membrane-associated light-harvesting pigment-protein complex of cyanobacteria and red algae, built from phycobiliprotein core and rod cylinders plus linker polypeptides, that funnels phycobilin excitation energy to photosynthetic reaction centers.

label: plasma membrane-derived photosystem I
definition: A photosystem I protein complex located in the plasma membrane-derived bacterial thylakoid membrane.

label: plasma membrane-derived thylakoid photosystem II
definition: A photosystem II protein complex located in the plasma membrane-derived bacterial thylakoid that contains a P680 reaction center and catalyzes the water-oxidizing, plastoquinone-reducing step of oxygenic photosynthesis.

label: proton-transporting ATP synthase complex
definition: The rotary motor enzyme that makes ATP from ADP and phosphate using the ion motive force across the membrane. It has two coupled sectors: a membrane-embedded Fo, whose c-ring turns as protons cross it, and a soluble F1 (alpha3beta3gammadeltaepsilon), whose catalytic beta subunits are driven through their conformational cycle by the rotating gamma subunit.

label: RC-LH1-PufX core complex
definition: A purple-bacterial chromatophore membrane protein complex that contains a photochemical reaction center, LH1 antenna proteins and PufX, receives excitation from surrounding LH2 antennae, and reduces quinone during cyclic photosynthetic electron transport.

label: vacuolar proton-transporting V-type ATPase complex
definition: A proton-transporting two-sector ATPase complex found in the vacuolar membrane, where it acts as a proton pump to mediate acidification of the vacuolar lumen.

label: vacuolar proton-transporting V-type ATPase, V0 domain
definition: The V0 domain of a proton-transporting V-type ATPase found in the vacuolar membrane.

label: vacuolar proton-transporting V-type ATPase, V1 domain
definition: The V1 domain of a proton-transporting V-type ATPase found in the vacuolar membrane.

label: capsule
definition: A highly organized glycocalyx layer attached outside the cell wall of some bacteria and fungi, usually built from capsular polysaccharides and retained on the cell surface rather than released as a loose extracellular polymer.

label: cell outer membrane
definition: The outermost lipid bilayer of a diderm cell envelope. In canonical Gram-negative bacteria it is asymmetric, with phospholipid enriched in the inner leaflet and lipopolysaccharide enriched in the outer leaflet, and contains beta-barrel proteins that mediate transport and assembly.

label: cellular bud membrane
definition: The specialized plasma-membrane region that surrounds a cellular bud.

label: dolipore septum
definition: A porous fungal cell septum in which the cross-wall swells around a central pore and the pore is capped on both sides by septal pore caps called parenthesomes.

label: eisosome membrane domain/MCC
definition: A plasma membrane part that is composed of a furrow-like plasma membrane domain and associated integral transmembrane proteins.

label: fungal-type cell wall
definition: A rigid but dynamic carbohydrate- and glycoprotein-rich wall surrounding the fungal plasma membrane, built from a variable cross-linked matrix of glucans, wall glycoproteins, and often chitin and kept distinct from fungal capsules outside the wall.

label: glycocalyx
definition: A carbohydrate rich layer at the outermost periphery of a cell.

label: Gram-negative-bacterium-type cell wall
definition: The relatively thin peptidoglycan layer of a Gram-negative cell envelope, located in the periplasm between the cytoplasmic and outer membranes and physically connected to the outer membrane by lipoproteins.

label: mycolate outer membrane
definition: A mycolic-acid-rich cell outer membrane in mycobacteria and related Corynebacteriales, containing a lipid bilayer and covalently linked long-chain mycolic acids attached to peptidoglycan through an arabinogalactan network.

label: outer membrane-bounded periplasmic space
definition: The region between the inner (cytoplasmic or plasma) membrane and outer membrane of organisms with two membranes such as Gram negative bacteria. These periplasmic spaces are relatively thick and contain a thin peptidoglycan layer (PGL), also referred to as a thin cell wall.

label: peptidoglycan-based cell wall
definition: A protective, load-bearing structure outside the cytoplasmic membrane, built from glycan strands of alternating N-acetylglucosamine and N-acetylmuramic acid cross-linked by short peptides. The resulting murein sacculus surrounds the cell and resists turgor pressure.

label: plasma membrane
definition: The lipid membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cytoplasm from the external environment and houses proteins for selective transport, signaling, and envelope biogenesis.

label: S-layer
definition: A paracrystalline monomolecular array of one or more (glyco)protein species that self-assemble on the outermost surface of the cell envelope, with oblique, square or hexagonal lattice symmetry. S-layers are common in Archaea, where they are often the sole wall component, and widespread but patchily distributed in Bacteria.

label: slime layer
definition: A slime layer is an easily removed, diffuse, unorganized layer of extracellular material that surrounds a cell. Specifically this consists mostly of exopolysaccharides, glycoproteins, and glycolipids.

label: cyanophycin granule
definition: A bacterial storage inclusion in which insoluble cyanophycin polymer accumulates as cytoplasmic granules that store fixed nitrogen and carbon for later mobilization.

label: gas vesicle
definition: A gas-filled, non-membrane-bounded protein organelle, usually shaped as a cylindrical shell with conical end caps. Its gas-permeable, water-excluding wall lowers cell density and enables buoyancy regulation in aquatic microbes.

label: gas vesicle shell
definition: The proteinaceous structure surrounding a gas vesicle.

label: glycogen granule
definition: A microbial carbohydrate storage inclusion in which glycogen polymer accumulates as cytoplasmic granules that store glucose-derived carbon and energy for later mobilization.

label: lipid droplet
definition: An intracellular non-membrane-bounded organelle comprising a matrix of coalesced lipids surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer. May include associated proteins.

label: monolayer-surrounded lipid storage body outer lipid monolayer
definition: The single layer of phospholipids surrounding a lipid storage body.

label: plastoglobule
definition: A lipoprotein particle present in chloroplasts.

label: polyhydroxyalkanoate granule
definition: A cytoplasmic prokaryotic inclusion body in which polyhydroxyalkanoate storage polymers condense with granule-associated proteins, including PHA synthases and phasins, to form hydrophobic carbon- and reducing-power storage granules.

label: R-body
definition: A bacterial proteinaceous inclusion body assembled from Reb proteins that forms a coiled ribbon and can extend into a hollow tube.

label: sulfur globule
definition: A bacterial sulfur storage inclusion that accumulates elemental sulfur from reduced sulfur compounds and packages it with sulfur-globule envelope proteins for temporary storage and later oxidation.

label: acidocalcisome
definition: An acidic electron-dense membrane-bounded organelle found in diverse microbes that stores polyphosphate, pyrophosphate, calcium and other cations and uses proton pumps and cation transporters to maintain its ion-rich matrix.

label: acidocalcisome lumen
definition: The acidocalcisome compartment bounded by the acidocalcisomal membrane.

label: acidocalcisome membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding an acidocalcisome.

label: anammoxosome
definition: A ladderane-lipid-bounded intracytoplasmic organelle of anaerobic ammonium-oxidizing Planctomycetota that localizes the hydrazine-producing anammox catabolic pathway and its energy-conserving membrane reactions.

label: anammoxosome membrane
definition: The single ladderane-lipid-containing bilayer membrane that surrounds the anammoxosome.

label: apicomplexan dense granule
definition: Electron-dense organelle with a granular internal matrix found in a apicomplexan parasite; contains proteins destined to be secreted into the parasitophorous vacuole following parasite invasion of a host cell.

label: apicomplexan dense granule membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a dense granule of the type found in apicomplexan parasites.

label: apicoplast
definition: The plastid organelle found in apicomplexans.

label: apicoplast membrane
definition: Any of the lipid bilayers that surround an apicoplast and form the apicoplast envelope.

label: autophagosome
definition: A double-membrane-bounded compartment that engulfs endogenous cellular material as well as invading microorganisms to target them to the lytic vacuole/lysosome for degradation as part of macroautophagy.

label: autophagosome lumen
definition: The volume enclosed within the autophagosome double-membrane.

label: autophagosome membrane
definition: The membrane surrounding the autophagosome.

label: bacterial thylakoid
definition: A thylakoid that is derived from and attached to, but not necessarily continuous with, the plasma membrane, and is not enclosed in a plastid. It bears the photosynthetic pigments in photosynthetic cyanobacteria.

label: chloroplast
definition: A chlorophyll-containing plastid with thylakoids organized into grana and frets, or stroma thylakoids, and embedded in a stroma.

label: chloroplast envelope
definition: The double lipid bilayer enclosing the chloroplast and separating its contents from the rest of the cytoplasm; includes the intermembrane space.

label: chloroplast inner membrane
definition: The inner, i.e. lumen-facing, lipid bilayer of the chloroplast envelope; also faces the chloroplast stroma.

label: chloroplast intermembrane space
definition: The region between the inner and outer lipid bilayers of a chloroplast envelope.

label: chloroplast membrane
definition: Either of the lipid bilayers that surround a chloroplast and form the chloroplast envelope.

label: chloroplast outer membrane
definition: The cytoplasm-facing lipid bilayer of the chloroplast envelope.

label: chloroplast stroma
definition: The internal space enclosed by the chloroplast double membrane but excluding the thylakoid space.

label: chloroplast thylakoid
definition: Sac-like membranous structures in a chloroplast combined into stacks, or grana, and present singly in the stroma as stroma thylakoids or frets that interconnect grana.

label: chloroplast thylakoid lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the membrane of a chloroplast thylakoid.

label: chloroplast thylakoid membrane
definition: The pigmented membrane of a chloroplast thylakoid.

label: chlorosome
definition: A large light-harvesting antenna organelle of green photosynthetic bacteria in which bacteriochlorophyll aggregates self-assemble inside a lipid envelope and attach to the cytoplasmic membrane through a bacteriochlorophyll a-containing CsmA baseplate.

label: chlorosome envelope
definition: The structure, composed of a monolayer of glycolipids with embedded proteins, that encloses the pigments and other contents of the chlorosome.

label: cis-Golgi network
definition: The network of interconnected tubular and cisternal structures located at the convex side of the Golgi apparatus, which abuts the endoplasmic reticulum.

label: cis-Golgi network membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments that make up the cis-Golgi network.

label: clathrin-coated endocytic vesicle
definition: A clathrin-coated, membrane-bounded intracellular vesicle formed by invagination of the plasma membrane around an extracellular substance.

label: clathrin-coated endocytic vesicle lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the membrane of a clathrin-coated endocytic vesicle.

label: clathrin-coated endocytic vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a clathrin-coated endocytic vesicle.

label: clathrin-coated vesicle
definition: A vesicle with a coat formed of clathrin connected to the membrane via one of the clathrin adaptor complexes.

label: clathrin-coated vesicle lumen
definition: The clathrin-coated vesicle compartment bounded by the clathrin-coated vesicle membrane.

label: clathrin-coated vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a clathrin-coated vesicle.

label: coated vesicle
definition: Small membrane-bounded organelle formed by pinching off of a coated region of membrane. Some coats are made of clathrin, whereas others are made from other proteins.

label: coated vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a coated vesicle.

label: contractile vacuolar membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the contractile vacuole.

label: contractile vacuole
definition: A specialized vacuole of eukaryotic cells, especially Protozoa, that fills with water from the cytoplasm and then discharges this externally by the opening of contractile vacuole pores. One of its functions is osmoregulatory.

label: contractile vacuole lumen
definition: The contractile vacuole compartment bounded by the contractile vacuole membrane.

label: COPI-coated vesicle
definition: A vesicle with a coat formed of the COPI coat complex proteins. COPI-coated vesicles are found associated with Golgi membranes at steady state, are involved in Golgi to endoplasmic reticulum (retrograde) vesicle transport, and possibly also in intra-Golgi transport.

label: COPI-coated vesicle lumen
definition: The COPI-coated vesicle compartment bounded by the COPI-coated vesicle membrane.

label: COPI-coated vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a COPI-coated vesicle.

label: COPII-coated ER to Golgi transport vesicle
definition: A vesicle with a coat formed of the COPII coat complex proteins. The COPII coat complex is formed by the Sec23p/Sec24p and the Sec13p/Sec31p heterodimers. COPII-associated vesicles transport proteins from the rough endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus (anterograde transport).

label: COPII-coated vesicle lumen
definition: The COPII-coated vesicle compartment bounded by the COPII-coated vesicle membrane.

label: Cvt vesicle
definition: A cytosolic vesicle that is enclosed by a double membrane and is implicated in the cytoplasm to vacuole targeting pathway. These vesicles are found in the yeast S. cerevisiae, and contain vacuolar hydrolases, aminopeptidase I (Ape1p) and alpha-mannosidase (Ams1p).

label: Cvt vesicle lumen
definition: The Cvt vesicle compartment bounded by the Cvt vesicle membrane.

label: Cvt vesicle membrane
definition: Either lipid bilayer membrane surrounding a Cvt vesicle, a double membrane-layered vesicle implicated in the cytoplasm to vacuole targeting pathway.

label: cyanelle
definition: A plastid that contains unstacked, phycobilisome-bearing thylakoid membranes and is surrounded by a double membrane with a peptidoglycan layer in the intermembrane space between the two envelope membranes. Cyanelles are characteristic of algae in the class Glaucophyta, and may represent an ancestral form of plastid.

label: cyanelle envelope
definition: The double lipid bilayer enclosing the cyanelle and separating its contents from the rest of the cytoplasm; includes the intermembrane space.

label: cyanelle inner membrane
definition: The inner, i.e. lumen-facing, lipid bilayer of the cyanelle envelope; also faces the cyanelle stroma.

label: cyanelle intermembrane space
definition: The region between the inner and outer lipid bilayers of the cyanelle envelope; includes the peptidoglycan layer.

label: cyanelle membrane
definition: Either of the lipid bilayers that surround a cyanelle and form the cyanelle envelope.

label: cyanelle outer membrane
definition: The outer, i.e. cytoplasm-facing, lipid bilayer of the cyanelle envelope.

label: cyanelle stroma
definition: The space enclosed by the double membrane of a cyanelle.

label: cyanelle thylakoid
definition: A thylakoid found in a cyanelle, which is a type of plastid found in certain algae. The cyanelle contains a photosynthetic membrane resembling that of cyanobacteria.

label: cyanelle thylakoid lumen
definition: The cyanelle compartment bounded by the thylakoid membranes.

label: cyanelle thylakoid membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer membrane of any thylakoid within a cyanelle, a photosynthetic organelle of glaucocystophyte algae.

label: cytoplasmic vesicle
definition: A vesicle found in the cytoplasm of a cell.

label: cytoplasmic vesicle lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by a cytoplasmic vesicle.

label: cytoplasmic vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a cytoplasmic vesicle.

label: endocytic vesicle
definition: A membrane-bounded intracellular vesicle formed by invagination of the plasma membrane around an extracellular substance. Endocytic vesicles fuse with early endosomes to deliver the cargo for further sorting.

label: endocytic vesicle lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the membrane of an endocytic vesicle.

label: endocytic vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding an endocytic vesicle.

label: endoplasmic reticulum
definition: The irregular network of unit membranes, visible only by electron microscopy, that occurs in the cytoplasm of many eukaryotic cells. The membranes form a complex meshwork of tubular channels, which are often expanded into slitlike cavities called cisternae. The ER takes two forms, rough (or granular), with ribosomes adhering to the outer surface, and smooth (with no ribosomes attached).

label: endoplasmic reticulum lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the membranes of the endoplasmic reticulum.

label: endoplasmic reticulum membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the endoplasmic reticulum.

label: endosome
definition: A vacuole to which materials ingested by endocytosis are delivered.

label: endosome lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the membrane of an endosome.

label: endosome membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding an endosome.

label: ER to Golgi transport vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a vesicle transporting substances from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus.

label: esterosome
definition: A vesicle filled with crystalline protein that shows sequence similarities with various esterases.

label: esterosome lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the esterosome membrane.

label: esterosome membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding an esterosome.

label: exoneme
definition: A dense granule-like organelle of the apical complex of merozoites, released into the parasitophorous vacuole, mediating protease-dependent rupture and parasite exit from the infected erythrocyte.

label: eyespot apparatus
definition: A small pigmented organelle used in single-celled organisms to detect light.

label: ferrosome
definition: A bacterial lipid-bounded iron-storage organelle that contains iron-, phosphorus- and oxygen-rich material and forms through Fez protein-dependent machinery.

label: flagellar pocket
definition: Invagination of the plasma membrane from which a flagellum protrudes.

label: food vacuole
definition: A vacuole within a parasite used for digestion of the host cell cytoplasm.

label: fungal-type vacuole
definition: A vacuole that has both lytic and storage functions. The fungal vacuole is a large, membrane-bounded organelle that functions as a reservoir for small molecules and as the primary compartment for degradation.

label: fungal-type vacuole lumen
definition: The volume enclosed within the vacuolar membrane of the fungal-type vacuole.

label: fungal-type vacuole membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the fungal-type vacuole.

label: glycosome
definition: A membrane-bounded organelle found in organisms from the order Kinetoplastida that houses the enzymes of glycolysis.

label: glycosome lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the glycosome membrane.

label: glycosome membrane
definition: The membrane surrounding the glycosome.

label: glyoxysomal lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the glyoxysome membrane.

label: glyoxysomal membrane
definition: The membrane surrounding the glyoxysome.

label: glyoxysome
definition: A specialized form of peroxisome that contains the enzymes of the glyoxylate pathway. The glyoxysome is found in some plant cells, notably the cells of germinating seeds.

label: Golgi apparatus
definition: A membrane-bound cytoplasmic organelle of the endomembrane system that further processes the core oligosaccharides (e.g. N-glycans) added to proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum and packages them into membrane-bound vesicles. The Golgi apparatus operates at the intersection of the secretory, lysosomal, and endocytic pathways.

label: Golgi-associated vesicle
definition: Any vesicle associated with the Golgi complex and involved in mediating transport within the Golgi or between the Golgi and other parts of the cell.

label: Golgi-associated vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a vesicle associated with the Golgi apparatus.

label: Golgi cisterna
definition: Any of the thin, flattened membrane-bounded compartments that form the central portion of the Golgi complex.

label: Golgi cisterna membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the thin, flattened compartments that form the central portion of the Golgi complex.

label: Golgi membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments of the Golgi apparatus.

label: hydrogenosomal membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a hydrogenosome.

label: hydrogenosome
definition: A spherical, membrane-bounded organelle found in some anaerobic protozoa, which participates in ATP and molecular hydrogen formation.

label: hydrogenosome lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the hydrogenosome membrane.

label: inner membrane pellicle complex
definition: An apicomplexan double-membrane pellicle structure formed by flattened vesicles beneath the plasma membrane.

label: late endosome
definition: A prelysosomal endocytic organelle differentiated from early endosomes by lower lumenal pH and different protein composition. Late endosomes are more spherical than early endosomes and are mostly juxtanuclear, being concentrated near the microtubule organizing center.

label: magnetosome
definition: A membrane-bounded organelle of magnetotactic bacteria enclosing a nanocrystal of a magnetic iron mineral — magnetite (Fe3O4) or greigite (Fe3S4). Magnetosomes are invaginations of the cytoplasmic membrane that are filled with iron, and are arranged into a chain along a cytoskeletal filament so that the cell behaves as a swimming compass needle.

label: magnetosome lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the magnetosome membrane.

label: magnetosome membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer membrane surrounding a magnetosome.

label: Maurer's cleft
definition: A disk-like structure that appears at the periphery of a red blood cell infected by an apicomplexan parasite, characterized by a translucent lumen and an electron-dense coat of variable thickness; often appears to be tethered to the host cell membrane by fibrous connections with the erythrocyte cytoskeleton.

label: methane-oxidizing organelle
definition: A cytoplasmic, membrane-bounded organelle in aerobic methanotrophic bacteria, built from intracytoplasmic membranes that house particulate methane monooxygenase and associated electron-transfer proteins for methane catabolism.

label: microneme
definition: A small, elongated secretory organelle that forms part of the apical complex, located along the main axis of an apicomplexan parasite cell within the extreme apical region and at the periphery under the inner membrane complex. Of the specialized secretory compartments identified in apicomplexans, micronemes discharge their contents first, during initial contact of the parasite's apical pole with the host cell surface. Micronemal proteins function during parasite attachment and penetration into the target cell.

label: microneme lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the microneme membrane.

label: microneme membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a microneme.

label: microsporidian posterior vacuole
definition: A membrane-bounded posterior vesicle in a microsporidian spore that expands during germination and is implicated in polar-tube extrusion and sporoplasm expulsion.

label: mitochondrial crista
definition: Any of the inward folds of the mitochondrial inner membrane. Their number, extent, and shape differ in mitochondria from different tissues and organisms. They appear to be devices for increasing the surface area of the mitochondrial inner membrane, where the enzymes of electron transport and oxidative phosphorylation are found. Their shape can vary with the respiratory state of the mitochondria.

label: mitochondrial crista junction
definition: A tubular structure of relatively uniform size that connects a mitochondrial crista to the mitochondrial inner boundary membrane.

label: mitochondrial envelope
definition: The double lipid bilayer enclosing the mitochondrion and separating its contents from the cell cytoplasm; includes the intermembrane space.

label: mitochondrial inner membrane
definition: The inner, i.e. lumen-facing, lipid bilayer of the mitochondrial envelope. It is highly folded to form cristae.

label: mitochondrial intermembrane space
definition: The region between the inner and outer lipid bilayers of the mitochondrial envelope.

label: mitochondrial matrix
definition: The gel-like material, with considerable fine structure, that lies in the matrix space, or lumen, of a mitochondrion. It contains the enzymes of the tricarboxylic acid cycle and, in some organisms, the enzymes concerned with fatty acid oxidation.

label: mitochondrial membrane
definition: Either of the lipid bilayers that surround the mitochondrion and form the mitochondrial envelope.

label: mitochondrial outer membrane
definition: The outer, i.e. cytoplasm-facing, lipid bilayer of the mitochondrial envelope.

label: mitochondrion
definition: A semiautonomous, self replicating organelle that occurs in varying numbers, shapes, and sizes in the cytoplasm of virtually all eukaryotic cells. It is notably the site of tissue respiration.

label: mitosome
definition: A double-membrane-bounded organelle that functions in iron-sulfur protein maturation; evolutionarily derived from mitochondria. The mitosome has been detected only in anaerobic or microaerophilic organisms that do not have mitochondria, such as Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia intestinalis and several species of Microsporidia. These organisms are not capable of gaining energy from oxidative phosphorylation, which is normally performed by mitochondria.

label: mitosome envelope
definition: The mitosomal envelope comprises the inner and outer mitosomal membrane including the intermembrane space.

label: mitosome inner membrane
definition: The inner membrane of a mitosome is the membrane which separates the mitosomal matrix from the intermembrane space.

label: mitosome intermembrane space
definition: The mitosomal intermembrane space is the space between inner and outer mitosomal membranes.

label: mitosome matrix
definition: The matrix of a mitosome is the mitosomal internal spaces enclosed by the inner membrane.

label: mitosome outer membrane
definition: The outer membrane of a mitosome is the mitosomal membrane facing the cytoplasm.

label: mucocyst
definition: A small subcellular vesicle, surrounded by a membrane, in the pellicle of ciliate protozoans that discharges a mucus-like secretion.

label: multivesicular body
definition: A type of endosome in which regions of the limiting endosomal membrane invaginate to form internal vesicles; membrane proteins that enter the internal vesicles are sequestered from the cytoplasm.

label: multivesicular body lumen
definition: The multivesicular body compartment bounded by the multivesicular body membrane.

label: multivesicular body membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a multivesicular body.

label: nuclear envelope
definition: The double lipid bilayer that encloses the nucleus, separating its contents from the cytoplasm. It consists of an inner and outer nuclear membrane, with an intermembrane space (20-40 nm wide, also called the perinuclear space) between them. The envelope is supported by the nuclear lamina and contains nuclear pore complexes, which regulate molecular transport.

label: nuclear envelope lumen
definition: The region between the two lipid bilayers of the nuclear envelope.

label: nuclear inner membrane
definition: The inner, i.e. lumen-facing, lipid bilayer of the nuclear envelope.

label: nuclear lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the nuclear inner membrane.

label: nuclear outer membrane
definition: The outer, i.e. cytoplasm-facing, lipid bilayer of the nuclear envelope.

label: nucleomorph
definition: A small, vestigial nucleus found in some plastids that derive from a eukaryotic endosymbiont. Observed in chlorarachniophytes and cryptomonads, which acquired their plastids from a green and red alga respectively.

label: nucleus
definition: A membrane-bounded organelle of eukaryotic cells in which chromosomes are housed and replicated. In most cells, the nucleus contains all of the cell's chromosomes except the organellar chromosomes, and is the site of RNA synthesis and processing.

label: organellar chromatophore
definition: A bacteroid-containing symbiosome in which the bacterial component is a genetically highly reduced cyanobacterium that is photosynthetically active

label: organellar chromatophore inner membrane
definition: The inner, i.e. lumen-facing, of the two lipid bilayers surrounding an organellar chromatophore.

label: organellar chromatophore intermembrane space
definition: The region between the inner and outer lipid bilayers that surround an organellar chromatophore.

label: organellar chromatophore membrane
definition: Either of the lipid bilayers that surround an organellar chromatophore.

label: organellar chromatophore outer membrane
definition: The outer, i.e. cytoplasm-facing, of the two lipid bilayers surrounding an organellar chromatophore.

label: organellar chromatophore thylakoid
definition: A thylakoid located in an organellar chromatophore

label: organellar chromatophore thylakoid lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by an organellar chromatophore thylakoid membrane.

label: organellar chromatophore thylakoid membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer membrane of any thylakoid within an organellar chromatophore.

label: parasitophorous vacuole
definition: A membrane-bounded host-cell vacuole in which an invading apicomplexan parasite resides and develops; its bounding parasitophorous vacuolar membrane is initiated during host-cell invasion and surrounds the intracellular parasite.

label: parasitophorous vacuole lumen
definition: The parasitophorous vacuole compartment bounded by the membrane of the parasitophorous vacuole.

label: parasitophorous vacuole membrane
definition: The membrane surrounding the parasitophorous vacuole.

label: peroxisomal matrix
definition: The volume contained within the membranes of a peroxisome; in many cells the matrix contains a crystalloid core largely composed of urate oxidase.

label: peroxisomal membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a peroxisome.

label: peroxisome
definition: A small organelle enclosed by a single membrane, and found in most eukaryotic cells; it contains peroxidases and other enzymes involved in metabolic processes including free radical detoxification, lipid catabolism and biosynthesis, and hydrogen peroxide metabolism.

label: photosynthetic membrane
definition: A membrane enriched in complexes formed of reaction centers, accessory pigments and electron carriers, in which photosynthetic reactions take place.

label: plasma membrane-derived chromatophore membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer associated with a plasma membrane-derived chromatophore; surrounds chromatophores that form complete vesicles.

label: plasma membrane-derived thylakoid lumen
definition: The internal lumen enclosed by a plasma membrane-derived bacterial thylakoid.

label: plasma membrane-derived thylakoid membrane
definition: The pigmented membrane of a plasma membrane-derived thylakoid.

label: plastid
definition: Any member of a family of organelles found in the cytoplasm of plants and some protists, which are membrane-bounded and contain DNA. Plant plastids develop from a common type, the proplastid.

label: plastid envelope
definition: The double lipid bilayer enclosing a plastid and separating its contents from the rest of the cytoplasm; includes the intermembrane space.

label: plastid inner membrane
definition: The inner, i.e. lumen-facing, lipid bilayer of the plastid envelope; also faces the plastid stroma.

label: plastid intermembrane space
definition: The region between the inner and outer lipid bilayers of the plastid envelope.

label: plastid membrane
definition: Any lipid bilayer that surrounds a plastid or is part of the plastid envelope. Primary plastids (in plants, green algae, red algae, and glaucophytes) are surrounded by two membranes; complex plastids derived from secondary endosymbiosis are surrounded by three or four membranes.

label: plastid outer membrane
definition: The outer, i.e. cytoplasm-facing, lipid bilayer of the plastid envelope.

label: plastid stroma
definition: The ground substance of a plastid.

label: plastid thylakoid
definition: Any thylakoid within a plastid.

label: plastid thylakoid lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by a plastid thylakoid membrane.

label: plastid thylakoid membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer membrane of any thylakoid within a plastid.

label: polaroplast
definition: A membrane-bounded organelle found in a microsporidian spore that swells with water and exerts pressure to rupture the polar cap and evert the polar tube.

label: pyrenoid tubule
definition: A specialized membranous structure that extends from the photosynthetic thylakoid membrane into and transverses the matrix of a pyrenoid.

label: reservosome
definition: A posterior, membrane-bounded endocytic organelle in Trypanosoma cruzi epimastigotes that receives internalized macromolecular cargo.

label: rhoptry
definition: A large, club-shaped secretory organelle that forms part of the apical complex of an apicomplexan parasite, and consists of a bulbous body and a narrow electron-dense neck that extends through the conoid at the apical tip of the parasite. The rhoptry necks serve as ducts through which the contents of the rhoptries are secreted after attachment to the host has been completed and at the commencement of invasion. Rhoptry proteins function in the biogenesis and host organellar association of the parasitophorous vacuole.

label: rhoptry lumen
definition: The volume enclosed by the rhoptry membrane.

label: rhoptry membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a rhoptry.

label: rhoptry neck
definition: Narrow, electron-dense part of the rhoptry that extends through the conoid at the apical tip of an apicomplexan parasite.

label: spongiome
definition: A network of tubules and vesicles that is part of a contractile vacuole complex and participates in external water discharge during osmoregulation.

label: thylakoid
definition: A membranous cellular structure that bears the photosynthetic pigments in photosynthetic bacteria and within chloroplasts.

label: thylakoid membrane
definition: The pigmented photosynthetic membrane of cyanobacteria and chloroplasts, enriched in photosystems, cytochrome b6f, ATP synthase, plastoquinone and glycolipids, where light-driven electron transport builds the proton motive force for photosynthetic ATP synthesis.

label: trans-Golgi network
definition: The network of interconnected tubular and cisternal structures located within the Golgi apparatus on the side distal to the endoplasmic reticulum, from which secretory vesicles emerge. The trans-Golgi network is important in the later stages of protein secretion where it is thought to play a key role in the sorting and targeting of secreted proteins to the correct destination.

label: trans-Golgi network membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments that make up the trans-Golgi network.

label: trans-Golgi network transport vesicle membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding a vesicle transporting substances between the trans-Golgi network and other parts of the cell.

label: trichocyst
definition: A crystalline exocytotic organelle composed of small, acidic proteins existing primarily as disulphide-linked dimers. The trichocyst releases long filamentous proteins that capture predators in net-like structures to slow them down when the cell is disturbed.

label: vacuolar lumen
definition: The volume enclosed within the vacuolar membrane.

label: vacuolar membrane
definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the vacuole and separating its contents from the cytoplasm of the cell.

label: vacuole
definition: A closed structure, found only in eukaryotic cells, that is completely surrounded by unit membrane and contains liquid material.

label: Woronin body
definition: A peroxisome-derived dense-core vesicle of filamentous fungi that seals septal pores upon hyphal wounding.

label: bacterial microcompartment
definition: A bacterial protein-shelled organelle in which a selectively permeable polyhedral shell encapsulates pathway enzymes to segregate segments of metabolism from the cytosol.

label: carboxysome
definition: A bacterial microcompartment — a polyhedral, selectively permeable protein shell about 100–200 nm across — that encapsulates RuBisCO and carbonic anhydrase to concentrate CO2 around RuBisCO in cyanobacteria and many chemoautotrophs. Alpha-carboxysomes (cso genes) and beta-carboxysomes (ccm genes) evolved their shells and scaffolds independently.

label: carboxysome shell
definition: The polyhedral protein coat of alpha- and beta-carboxysomes, built from BMC-H, BMC-T, and BMC-P shell proteins that enclose RuBisCO and carbonic anhydrase while controlling metabolite traffic between the lumen and cytosol.

label: encapsulin nanocompartment
definition: A proteinaceous nanocompartment, 24 to 42 nm across, built from a single HK97-fold shell protein that self-assembles into an icosahedron. Cargo enzymes are packaged inside by a short targeting peptide that binds the shell interior; the commonest cargoes are ferritin-like iron-mineralising proteins and peroxidases.

label: ethanolamine degradation polyhedral organelle
definition: An organelle found in bacteria consisting of a proteinaceous coat containing enzymes for the degradation of ethanolamine whose purpose is the protection of the rest of the cell from the toxic acetaldehyde product of the enzyme ethanolamine ammonia lyase.

label: propanediol degradation polyhedral organelle
definition: An organelle found in bacteria consisting of a proteinaceous coat containing enzymes for the degradation of 1,2-propanediol whose purpose is the protection of the rest of the cell from the toxic propionaldehyde product of the enzyme diol dehydratase.

label: chloroplast nucleoid
definition: The region of a chloroplast to which the DNA is confined.

label: kinetoplast
definition: A sub-structure within the large single mitochondrion of kinetoplastid parasites and which is closely associated with the flagellar pocket and basal body of the flagellum.

label: mitochondrial nucleoid
definition: The region of a mitochondrion to which the DNA is confined.

label: nucleoid
definition: The non-membrane-bounded subcellular region in which a bacterial chromosome is compacted and organized with nucleoid-associated proteins while remaining dynamically coupled to transcription and replication.

label: plastid nucleoid
definition: A region of a plastid to which the DNA is confined.

label: 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase complex
definition: A protein complex that catalyzes the transfer of a glucose group from UDP-glucose to a (1->3)-beta-D-glucan chain.

label: AP-1 adaptor complex
definition: A heterotetrameric AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that consists of beta1, gamma, mu1 and sigma1 subunits and links clathrin to the membrane surface of a vesicle; vesicles with AP-1-containing coats are normally found primarily in the trans-Golgi network. In at least humans, the AP-1 complex can be heterogeneric due to the existence of multiple subunit isoforms encoded by different genes (gamma1 and gamma2, mu1A and mu1B, and sigma1A, sigma1B and sigma1C).

label: AP-2 adaptor complex
definition: A heterotetrameric AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that consists of alpha, beta2, mu2 and sigma2 subunits, and links clathrin to the membrane surface of a vesicle, and the cargo receptors during receptor/clathrin mediated endocytosis. Vesicles with AP-2-containing coats are normally found primarily near the plasma membrane, on endocytic vesicles. In at least humans, the AP-2 complex can be heterogeneric due to the existence of multiple subunit isoforms encoded by different alpha genes (alphaA and alphaC).

label: AP-3 adaptor complex
definition: A heterotetrameric AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that consists of beta3, delta, mu3 and sigma3 subunits and is found associated with endosomal membranes. AP-3 does not appear to associate with clathrin in all organisms. In at least humans, the AP-3 complex can be heterogeneric due to the existence of multiple subunit isoforms encoded by different genes (beta3A and beta3B, mu3A and mu3B, and sigma3A and sigma3B).

label: AP-4 adaptor complex
definition: An AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that consists of beta4, epsilon, mu4 and sigma4 subunits and is found associated with membranes in the trans-Golgi network; it is not clear whether AP-4 forms clathrin coats in vivo.

label: AP-5 adaptor complex
definition: An AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that in humans consists of beta5, zeta, mu5 and sigma5 subunits and is found associated with membranes in the endosomes; it is not clear whether AP-5 forms clathrin coats in vivo.

label: AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex
definition: Any of several heterotetrameric complexes that link clathrin (or another coat-forming molecule, as hypothesized for AP-3 and AP-4) to a membrane surface; they are found on coated pits and coated vesicles, and mediate sorting of cargo proteins into vesicles. Each AP complex contains two large (a beta and one of either an alpha, gamma, delta, or epsilon) subunits (110-130 kDa), a medium (mu) subunit (approximately 50 kDa), and a small (sigma) subunit (15-20 kDa).

label: apical complex
definition: A group of cytoskeletal structures and associated membrane-bounded organelles at the anterior end of apicomplexan parasites that supports host-cell attachment, penetration, and parasite proliferation.

label: bacterial extracellular vesicle
definition: Small membrane vesicle (< 1 um) that buds off a prokaryotic cell plasma membrane, able to carry proteins, phospholipids, lipopolysaccharides, nucleic acids, viruses, and more. Important in intercellular communication and pathogenesis; can exist within host cells.

label: bacterial outer membrane vesicle
definition: A spherical, bilayered proteolipid vesicle released from gram-negative bacterial outer membranes.

label: Bam protein complex
definition: A bacterial outer-membrane beta-barrel protein assembly machine in which the BamA beta-barrel core and associated outer-membrane lipoproteins fold and insert beta-barrel proteins into the outer membrane.

label: CBF3 complex
definition: A multisubunit protein complex that binds to centromeric DNA and initiates kinetochore assembly. In yeast, this complex consists of four subunits, namely Ctf13p, Skp1p, Cep3p and Cbf2p.

label: cellular bud
definition: A cellular outgrowth formed during budding reproduction that remains connected to a mother cell while it grows into a new individual.

label: cellular bud neck
definition: The constricted cellular region between a mother cell and its daughter bud in budding organisms.

label: cellular bud tip
definition: The distal region of a cellular bud opposite the mother-cell attachment site.

label: cellulosome
definition: An extracellular membraneless organelle built around scaffoldin and dockerin-bearing enzymes that synergistically degrade insoluble plant-cell-wall polysaccharides.

label: chaperonin-containing T-complex
definition: A multisubunit ring-shaped complex that mediates protein folding in the cytosol without a cofactor.

label: clathrin coat
definition: A membrane coat found on coated pits and some coated vesicles; consists of polymerized clathrin triskelions, each comprising three clathrin heavy chains and three clathrin light chains, linked to the membrane via one of the AP adaptor complexes.

label: clathrin coat of coated pit
definition: The coat found on coated pits and the coated vesicles derived from coated pits; comprises clathrin and the AP-2 adaptor complex.

label: clathrin coat of endocytic vesicle
definition: A clathrin coat found on an endocytic vesicle.

label: clathrin coat of trans-Golgi network vesicle
definition: A clathrin coat found on a vesicle of the trans-Golgi network.

label: clathrin vesicle coat
definition: A membrane vesicle coat whose core lattice is built from clathrin and that coats clathrin-coated vesicles.

label: COG complex
definition: A multisubunit tethering complex of the CATCHR family (complexes associated with tethering containing helical rods) that has a role in tethering vesicles to the Golgi prior to fusion. Composed of 8 subunits COG1-8.

label: COMA complex
definition: A kinetochore multiprotein complex that bridges the subunits that are in contact with centromeric DNA and the subunits bound to microtubules during kinetochore assembly. In yeast, consists of Ctf19p, Okp1p, Mcm21p, and Ame1p.

label: COPI vesicle coat
definition: A COPI membrane vesicle coat complex found associated with Golgi membranes; it forms on COPI-coated vesicles that mediate Golgi-to-endoplasmic-reticulum retrograde transport.

label: COPII vesicle coat
definition: A COPII coat protein complex that assembles on endoplasmic-reticulum membranes to bud COPII-coated ER-to-Golgi transport vesicles; in budding yeast it contains Sar1p, Sec23p, Sec24p, Sec13p, and Sec31p.

label: CORVET complex
definition: A multimeric protein complex that acts as an endosomal tethering complex (CORVET = class C core vacuole/endosome tethering) by cooperating with Rab GTPases to capture endosomal vesicles and trap them prior to the action of SNAREs; the complex is involved in endo-lysosomal biogenesis and required for transport between endosome and vacuole. The Saccharomyces cerevisiae complex contains Vps8p, Vps3p, Pep5p, Vps16p, Pep3p, and Vps33p.

label: cytostome
definition: Stable, specialized structure for the ingestion of food by the cell into phagosomes.

label: DASH complex
definition: A large protein complex, containing around 8-10 subunits in yeast, including Duo1p, Dam1p, Dad1p and Ask1p. The complex forms part of the outer kinetochore, associates with microtubules when the kinetochore attaches to the spindle, and plays a role in spindle attachment, chromosome segregation and spindle stability.

label: Dsl1/NZR complex
definition: A multisubunit tethering complex, i.e. a protein complex involved in mediating the initial interaction between vesicles and the membranes with which they fuse, that is involved in trafficking from the Golgi apparatus to the ER. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae the Dsl1p complex contains Dsl1p, Tip20p, and Sec39p.

label: eisosome
definition: A cell part that is composed of the eisosome membrane or MCC domain, a furrow-like plasma membrane sub-domain and associated integral transmembrane proteins, and the proteins (eisosome filaments) that form a scaffolding lattice on the cytoplasmic face. Eisosomes broadly affect overall plasma membrane organization.

label: EMC complex
definition: A transmembrane protein complex in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane that promotes insertion of newly synthesized proteins into the ER membrane.

label: ERMES complex
definition: A protein complex that links the endoplasmic reticulum with mitochondria and may have a role in promoting exchange of calcium and phospholipids between the two organelles.

label: ESCRT-0 complex
definition: A protein complex required for the recycling of Golgi proteins, formation of lumenal membranes and sorting of ubiquitinated proteins into those membranes. This complex includes Vps1p and Hse1p in yeast and the Hrs and STAM proteins in mammals.

label: ESCRT I complex
definition: An endosomal sorting complex required for transport. It consists of the class E vacuolar protein sorting (Vps) proteins and interacts with ubiquitinated cargoes.

label: ESCRT II complex
definition: An endosomal sorting complex required for transport and functions downstream of ESCRT I complex. It consists of the class E vacuolar protein sorting (Vps) proteins and is required for the membrane recruitment of ESCRT III complex and binds to ubiquitinated cargoes.

label: ESCRT III complex
definition: A complex with membrane scission activity that plays a major role in many processes where membranes are remodelled - including endosomal transport (vesicle budding), nuclear envelope organisation (membrane closure, mitotic bridge cleavage), and cytokinesis (abscission).

label: exocyst
definition: A vesicle tethering complex peripherally associated with the plasma membrane that determines where vesicles dock and fuse. At least eight complex components are conserved between yeast and mammals.

label: exomer complex
definition: A protein complex that acts as a selective cargo adaptor mediating the selective transport of specific membrane proteins from the trans-Golgi network (TGN) to the plasma membrane.

label: GARP complex
definition: A quatrefoil tethering complex required for retrograde traffic from the early endosome back to the late Golgi and biogenesis of cytoplasmic vesicles.

label: GATOR1 complex
definition: A GTPase-activating protein (GAP) complex that regulates TORC1 signaling by interacting with the Rag GTPase. In human, the GATOR1 complex consists of DEPDC5, NPRL2, and NPRL3. In S. cerevisiae, this complex is referred to as SEACIT and contains the Iml1p, Npr2p, and Npr3p proteins.

label: GATOR2 complex
definition: A multiprotein subcomplex of the GATOR complex that regulates TORC1 signaling by interacting with the Rag GTPase. In human, this complex consists of WDR24, WDR59, MIOS, SEH1L, and SEC13. In S. cerevisiae, this complex is referred to as SEACAT and contains the Sea2p, Sea3p, Sea4p, Seh1p, Sec13p proteins.

label: GET complex
definition: An endoplasmic reticulum protein-containing complex that is conserved in eukaryotes and mediates the insertion of tail-anchored proteins into the ER membrane.

label: GPI-anchor transamidase complex
definition: A multisubunit membrane protein complex that attaches preassembled glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchors to proteins.

label: Gtr1-Gtr2 GTPase complex
definition: A heterodimer GTPase complex. In S. cerevisiae, this complex contains Gtr1p and Gtr2p proteins.

label: holdfast
definition: A polar extracellular adhesive matrix of Caulobacter vibrioides composed of secreted holdfast polysaccharide that is anchored at the old cell pole or stalk tip and enables irreversible surface attachment.

label: HOPS complex
definition: A multimeric protein complex that associates with the vacuolar membrane, late endosomal (multivesicular body) and lysosomal membranes. HOPS is a tethering complex involved in vesicle fusion.

label: kinetochore
definition: A multisubunit complex that is located at the centromeric region of DNA and provides an attachment point for the spindle microtubules.

label: membrane coat
definition: Any of several different proteinaceous coats that can associate with membranes. Membrane coats include those formed by clathrin plus an adaptor complex, the COPI and COPII complexes, and possibly others. They are found associated with membranes on many vesicles as well as other membrane features such as pits and perhaps tubules.

label: methyl accepting chemotaxis protein complex
definition: The chemoreceptor array: a hexagonal lattice of trimers-of-dimers of methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins, held at the membrane by the CheA kinase and the CheW coupling protein. The array is the cell's sensory organ, and its geometry — a 12 nm hexagonal spacing conserved across bacteria and archaea — is what gives chemotaxis its cooperativity and gain.

label: MICOS complex
definition: Mitochondrial inner membrane complex involved in maintenance of crista junctions, inner membrane architecture, and formation of contact sites to the outer membrane.

label: MIS12/MIND type complex
definition: A multiprotein kinetochore subcomplex that binds to centromeric chromatin and forms part of the outer kinetochore. It helps to recruit outer kinetochore subunits that will bind to microtubules. In humans, it consists of MIS12, DSN1, NSL1 and PMF1.

label: mitochondrial inner membrane peptidase complex
definition: Protease complex of the mitochondrial inner membrane, consisting of at least two subunits, involved in processing of both nuclear- and mitochondrially-encoded proteins targeted to the intermembrane space.

label: mitochondrial outer membrane translocase complex
definition: A large complex of the mitochondrial outer membrane that mediates transport of proteins into all mitochondrial compartments.

label: mitochondrial prohibitin complex
definition: Inner-mitochondrial-membrane macromolecular complex composed of repeating prohibitin 1 and prohibitin 2 heterodimeric subunits.

label: monopolin complex
definition: A protein complex required for clamping microtubule binding sites, ensuring orientation of sister kinetochores to the same pole (mono-orientation) during meiosis I.

label: Ndc80 complex
definition: A protein complex conserved among eukaryotes that forms part of the kinetochore and plays an essential role in forming stable kinetochore-microtubule attachments. The complex contains proteins known in several species, including budding and fission yeasts, as Ndc80p, Nuf2p, Spc24p, and Spc25p. In vertebrates it is part of the outer plate of the kinetochore.

label: nuclear chromosome
definition: A chromosome that encodes the nuclear genome and is found in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell during the cell cycle phases when the nucleus is intact.

label: nuclear pore
definition: A membrane-embedded eukaryotic protein complex that forms a discrete pore in the nuclear envelope where the inner and outer nuclear membranes join and mediates exchange between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

label: nuclear pore central transport channel
definition: A central eukaryotic nuclear pore substructure composed of FG-repeat channel nucleoporins that forms the selective transport path for RNAs, proteins, and small molecules.

label: nuclear pore cytoplasmic filaments
definition: Filamentous extensions on the cytoplasmic face of the eukaryotic nuclear pore complex.

label: nuclear pore inner ring
definition: A ring-shaped eukaryotic nuclear pore subcomplex built from inner-ring scaffold nucleoporins around the central transport channel.

label: nuclear pore linkers
definition: A eukaryotic nuclear pore substructure made of linker nucleoporins that connect central transport-channel FG nucleoporins with core nuclear-pore scaffold modules.

label: nuclear pore nuclear basket
definition: A filamentous, cage-like assembly on the nuclear face of the nuclear pore complex.

label: nuclear pore outer ring
definition: A ring-shaped eukaryotic nuclear pore subcomplex built from outer-ring coat nucleoporins on the cytoplasmic and nucleoplasmic faces of the nuclear pore scaffold.

label: nucleolus
definition: A dense, non-membrane-bounded body in the eukaryotic nuclear lumen that concentrates ribosomal DNA transcription, pre-rRNA processing, and early ribosomal subunit assembly.

label: PAM complex, Tim23 associated import motor
definition: A mitochondrial matrix-side protein complex associated with the TIM23 inner-membrane translocase that uses ATPase motor activity to drive protein import into the mitochondrial matrix.

label: phage nucleus
definition: A jumbo-bacteriophage protein-shelled compartment that assembles in infected bacterial cells, surrounds replicating phage DNA, and spatially separates phage genome replication and transcription from bacterial translation.

label: phagophore assembly site
definition: Punctate structures proximal to the endoplasmic reticulum which are the sites where the Atg machinery assembles upon autophagy induction.

label: polarisome
definition: A fungal cell-polarity protein complex that localizes to sites of polarized growth and directs localized actin-filament assembly, including the Saccharomyces Bni1/Spa2/Pea2/Bud6 polarisome.

label: PopZ polar microdomain
definition: A proteinaceous bacterial polar microdomain formed by PopZ polymers at Caulobacter cell poles that anchors the ParB-bound chromosomal origin and organizes pole-specific client proteins.

label: proteasome accessory complex
definition: A protein complex, that caps one or both ends of the proteasome core complex and regulates entry into, or exit from, the proteasome core complex.

label: proteasome complex
definition: A large multisubunit complex which catalyzes protein degradation, found in eukaryotes, archaea and some bacteria. In eukaryotes, this complex consists of the barrel shaped proteasome core complex and one or two associated proteins or complexes that act in regulating entry into or exit from the core.

label: proteasome core complex
definition: A barrel-shaped self-compartmentalized protease core of proteasomes, built from stacked alpha- and beta-subunit rings that sequester threonine protease active sites in an internal chamber for protein degradation.

label: pyrenoid
definition: A non-membrane-bounded organelle found within the chloroplasts of algae and hornworts; responsible for carbon dioxide fixation.

label: Ragulator complex
definition: A vacuolar membrane-anchored guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) complex for the Rag GTPases (Gtr1-Gtr2 GTPase complex GO:1990131) in TORC1 signaling pathway.
