In human, Ragulator is comprised of the membrane anchor subunit LAMTOR1 (Meh1p in S. cerevisiae, Lam1 in S. pombe), a GEF subunit LAMTOR2 ( Slm4 in S. cerevisiae , Lam2 in S. pombe ) , LAMTOR3 (no S. cerevisiae ortholog identified, Lam3 in S. pombe) , LAMTOR4 (no S. cerevisiae ortholog identified, Lam4 in S. pombe), and LAMTOR5 (no S. cerevisiae or S. pombe ortholog identified).

label: RAVE complex
definition: A multisubunit complex that in Saccharomyces is composed of three subunits, Rav1p, Rav2p and Skp1p. Acts transiently to catalyze assembly of cytoplasmic V1 with membrane embedded V0 to form the V-ATPase holoenzyme.

label: retromer complex
definition: A conserved hetero-pentameric membrane-associated complex involved in retrograde transport from endosomes to the Golgi apparatus. The budding yeast retromer comprises Vps35p, Vps29p, Vps26p, Vps5p, and Vps17p. The mammalian complex shows slight variation in composition compared to yeast, and comprises SNX1 or SNX2, SNX5 or SNX6, VPS26A or VPS26B, VPS29, and VPS35.

label: SAM complex
definition: A large complex of the mitochondrial outer membrane that mediates sorting of some imported proteins to the outer membrane and their assembly in the membrane; functions after import of incoming proteins by the mitochondrial outer membrane translocase complex.

label: Sec61 translocon complex
definition: A heterotrimeric endoplasmic-reticulum membrane translocon that forms a protein-conducting channel for co- and post-translational substrate movement across or into the ER membrane.

label: Sec62/Sec63 complex
definition: An endoplasmic-reticulum protein complex that supports posttranslational targeting of proteins to the ER and is represented in yeast by a Sec62p, Sec63p, Sec71p, and Sec72p tetramer.

label: Seh1-associated complex
definition: A GTPase-activating protein (GAP) complex that regulates TORC1 signaling by interacting with the Rag GTPase. In S. cerevisiae the complex contains Seh1p, Sec13p, Npr2p, Npr3p, Iml1p, Mtc5p, Rtc1p, and Sea4p.

label: spitzenkorper
definition: A structure within the hyphal tip of filamentous fungi that acts as an organizing center for hyphal growth.

label: Ssh1 translocon complex
definition: An endoplasmic-reticulum translocon complex with a core heterotrimer of alpha, beta, and gamma subunits, represented in budding yeast by Ssh1p, Sbh2p, and Sss1p, that supports cotranslational protein transport across the ER membrane.

label: Tic complex
definition: A chloroplast inner-envelope protein translocon complex that forms the inner-membrane step of nuclear-encoded preprotein import into the chloroplast.

label: TIM22 mitochondrial import inner membrane insertion complex
definition: A multi-subunit mitochondrial inner-membrane complex that mediates insertion of multi-pass inner-membrane precursor proteins carrying internal targeting elements.

label: TIM23 mitochondrial import inner membrane translocase complex
definition: The protein transport machinery of the mitochondrial inner membrane that typically transports proteins that possess a matrix-targeting N-terminal presequence. The TIM23 complex contains three essential Tim proteins: Tim17 and Tim23 are thought to build a preprotein translocation channel while Tim44 interacts transiently with the matrix heat-shock protein Hsp70 to form an ATP-driven import motor.

label: Toc complex
definition: A chloroplast outer-envelope protein translocon complex that forms the outer-membrane step of nuclear-encoded preprotein import into the chloroplast.

label: TORC1 complex
definition: A protein complex that contains at least TOR (target of rapamycin) and Raptor (regulatory-associated protein of TOR), or orthologs of, in complex with other signaling components. Mediates the phosphorylation and activation of S6K. In Saccharomyces, the complex contains Kog1p, Lst8p, Tco89p, and either Tor1p or Tor2p.

label: TORC2 complex
definition: A protein complex that contains at least TOR (target of rapamycin) and Rictor (rapamycin-insensitive companion of TOR), or orthologs of, in complex with other signaling components. Mediates the phosphorylation and activation of PKB (also called AKT). In Saccharomyces, the complex contains Avo1p, Avo2p, Tsc11p, Lst8p, Bit61p, Slm1p, Slm2p, and Tor2p.

label: TRAPPI protein complex
definition: A complex that tethers COPII vesicles at ER-Golgi intermediate compartment. Its role in this part of the vesicular transport may start at the ER exit sites. Binds to a component of the COPII coat. In yeast it includes the following subunits: Bet3 (as homodimer), Bet5, Trs20, Trs23, Trs31, Trs33 which are regarded as the core subunits of all TRAPP complexes in yeast.

label: TRAPPII protein complex
definition: A complex that mediates intra-Golgi traffic, Golgi exit, endosome-to-Golgi traffic, and the trafficking of autophagy proteins from Golgi to the phagophore assembly site. Binds to a component of the COPI coat. In yeast it includes the following subunits: Bet3 (as homodimer), Bet5, Tca17, Trs20, Trs23, Trs31, Trs33, Trs65, Trs120, Trs130. The whole complex is thought to dimerize with itself.

label: TRAPPIII protein complex
definition: A complex that functions in anterograde transport at the Golgi and also regulates autophagy. In yeast it includes at least the following subunits: Bet3 (as homodimer), Bet5, Trs20, Trs23, Trs31, Trs33, Trs85. TRAPPIII may include further, as yet undescribed, proteins.

label: vesicle coat
definition: A membrane coat found on a coated vesicle.

label: bacterial degradosome
definition: The degradosome is a protein complex playing a key role in mRNA degradation and RNA processing. It includes a RNA helicase, a 3'-5' phosphate-dependent PNPase and a RNase E bound-enolase.

label: cytoplasmic stress granule
definition: A dense aggregation in the cytosol composed of proteins and RNAs that appear when the cell is under stress.

label: exosome (RNase complex)
definition: A ribonuclease complex with 3'-to-5' exoribonuclease activity that participates in RNA processing and degradation.

label: large ribosomal subunit
definition: The larger of the two subunits of a ribosome. Two sites on the ribosomal large subunit are involved in translation, namely the aminoacyl site (A site) and peptidyl site (P site).

label: P-body
definition: A focus in the cytoplasm where mRNAs may become inactivated by decapping or some other mechanism. Protein and RNA localized to these foci are involved in mRNA degradation, nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD), translational repression, and RNA-mediated gene silencing.

label: ribosome
definition: The ribonucleoprotein particle that translates mRNA into protein. The bacterial and archaeal 70S ribosome comprises a small (30S) subunit built on 16S rRNA, which decodes the mRNA, and a large (50S) subunit built on 23S and 5S rRNA, whose 23S rRNA catalyses peptide bond formation. This record details that 70S form and the functional core shared with the larger eukaryotic cytosolic 80S ribosome; it does not enumerate 80S-specific components.

label: small ribosomal subunit
definition: The smaller of the two subunits of a ribosome.

label: ESX-3 type VII secretion system membrane complex
definition: A Mycobacterium smegmatis ESX-3 type VII secretion inner-membrane core complex in which EccB3, EccC3, EccD3, and EccE3 assemble into a dimeric membrane-embedded secretion machine.

label: ESX-5 type VII secretion system membrane complex
definition: A mycobacterial ESX-5 type VII secretion inner-membrane complex in which EccB5, EccC5, EccD5, EccE5, and MycP5 assemble into a multi-megadalton nanomachine that exports Esx and PE/PPE-family protein substrates.

label: SecYEG translocon complex
definition: A bacterial cytoplasmic-membrane Sec-pathway protein-conducting channel built from SecY, SecE, and SecG, through which unfolded secretory proteins or nascent membrane proteins move during translocation or membrane insertion.

label: TAT protein transport complex
definition: A complex of three proteins integral to the cytoplasmic membrane of bacteria and membranes of organelles derived from bacteria (chloroplasts and mitochondria) involved in membrane transport of folded proteins.

label: type I protein secretion system complex
definition: A Gram-negative bacterial trans-envelope protein secretion complex in which an inner-membrane ABC transporter and membrane-fusion protein recruit a TolC-like outer-membrane channel for one-step export of C-terminal-signal substrates.

label: type II protein secretion system complex
definition: A Gram-negative bacterial envelope-spanning secretion complex in which an inner-membrane platform and ATPase drive pseudopilus-mediated export of folded periplasmic substrates through an outer-membrane secretin.

label: type III protein secretion system complex
definition: The injectisome: a syringe-like envelope-spanning machine that delivers effector proteins from the bacterial cytoplasm directly into a eukaryotic host cell. Rings in the inner and outer membranes surround an export apparatus; an extracellular needle carries the secretion channel to a translocon pore in the host membrane. It is evolutionarily related to the flagellar export apparatus.

label: type IV secretion system complex
definition: A bacterial envelope-spanning secretion complex related to conjugation machines that uses VirB-family channel, pilus, ATPase and coupling-protein subassemblies to translocate DNA and protein substrates.

label: type IX protein secretion system complex
definition: A Bacteroidota trans-envelope secretion nanomachine that couples an inner-membrane PorL/PorM-family motor to PorK/PorN outer-membrane rings and a SprA/Sov translocon to export folded C-terminal-domain-bearing proteins across the outer membrane.

label: type VI protein secretion system complex
definition: A bacterial contractile injection machine whose envelope-spanning membrane complex anchors a baseplate and sheath-wrapped Hcp tube; sheath contraction propels the Hcp/VgrG/PAAR spike and associated effectors out of the cell into target cells.

label: endospore coat
definition: The layer in a bacterial endospore that lies under the exosporium, and is impermeable to many toxic molecules. The coat may also contain enzymes that are involved in endospore germination.

label: endospore cortex
definition: The thick, loosely cross-linked peptidoglycan layer between the spore core and the coat of a mature bacterial endospore.

label: endospore external encapsulating structure
definition: The layered envelope that surrounds a bacterial endospore and gives it its resistance: a thick modified peptidoglycan cortex, a proteinaceous coat of dozens of proteins outside it, and in some species an additional loose exosporium. It encases the dehydrated, mineralised core in which the chromosome is held.

label: microsporidian-type endospore
definition: The middle layer in a microsporidian spore wall that lies under the exospore and outside the plasma membrane, containing chitin and proteins.

label: microsporidian-type exospore
definition: The dense, protein-rich outermost layer of a microsporidian spore wall that lies above the endospore.

label: outer endospore membrane
definition: The outer membrane around a bacterial endospore, located between the endospore cortex and the endospore coat.

label: polar tube
definition: A microsporidian invasion tube that is coiled inside the spore as the polar filament and rapidly everts from the anterior pole during germination, forming a conduit for the sporoplasm toward a host cell.

label: polar tube anchoring disc
definition: A structural component of the microsporidian spore's invasion apparatus that is located at the anterior end of the spore and serves to attach the polar tube to the inside of the spore wall.

label: prospore membrane
definition: An ascospore-forming fungal double-membrane structure that grows from meiotic outer plaques to encapsulate meiotic nuclei and provide the foundation for spore-wall assembly.

label: prospore membrane leading edge
definition: The region of the prospore membrane that extends to surround the spore nucleus; coated with specific proteins that are thought to play a role in prospore membrane organization.

label: prospore membrane spindle pole body attachment site
definition: The region of the prospore membrane to which the spindle pole body (SPB) is anchored; the prospore membrane extends from the SPB attachment site to surround the spore nucleus.
